# 02 The shapes drawn with a path

## Outcome

`A{{Hexagon}}`, `A[/Para/]`, `A[\Alt\]`, `A[/Trap\]`, `A[\Trap/]` and `A>Flag]` draw the shapes
they name.

## Why this ticket exists

Six shapes, one drawing technique: a `<path>` of straight segments, sized by the same
fits-inside rule ticket 01 established for the rhombus. Grouped by technique rather than by
pipeline stage because board 4's policy forbids the horizontal slice — a shape parsed but drawn as
a rectangle is a silent mis-render.

Five of the six are in board 4's named-shape table; `A>Flag]` is not, and reaches only the generic
"Unrecognized flowchart line". Whichever of these tickets empties that table should delete it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] All six parse to their `NodeShape`, draw as a `<path class="siren-node-frame">`, and size so
      the label fits inside — the rule ticket 01 chose, applied, not reinvented.
- [x] **The two parallelograms lean opposite ways, and the two trapezoids do too.** Assert the
      geometry distinguishes them; a test that only checks "a path was drawn" would pass with all
      four identical, which is the same class of bug board 4's corpus exists to catch.
- [x] `A>Flag]` — the asymmetric shape — is right-pointing per Mermaid. **Measure it with the
      probe** (`pnpm --filter @siren/core probe`) rather than recalling which way it points.
- [x] Board 4's `UNIMPLEMENTED_BRACKET_FORMS` loses the five rows this ticket implements. If that
      empties the table, delete the table and its lookup; if not, say what is left and which ticket
      takes it.
- [x] Each shape still takes an author style and still animates.
- [x] Six corpus rows move to `supported`, each asserting its drawn shape. `REJECTED` 32 → **26**;
      `SILENTLY_WRONG` untouched at **3**.

- [x] **Carried from ticket 01, which found it and could not fix it.** `splitOutsideLabel` tracks
      `[`/`]` and the quote fence but not `{`/`}`, so `A{a-->b}` — valid Mermaid, a diamond
      labelled `a-->b`, measured with the probe — is cut at the arrow and refused, while
      `A["a-->b"]` works. Two spellings of one idea disagreeing. The fix is one more depth counter
      in that function. Add a corpus row for it and move the literal; the number rising because a
      gap was measured is progress, not regression.

## On the ratchet numbers in this ticket

They are an **expectation, not a quota.** Ticket 01 found a real compatibility gap and declined to
fix it because adding a corpus row would have pushed `REJECTED` one above the number its ticket
named. That was an honest reading of a badly written instruction: the ratchet exists to stop
regressions, not to stop progress.

So: if you discover a gap, **add the row and say so**. `rejected` rising because a new gap was
measured is the same legitimate case as `silently-wrong` rising in board 4 — a measurement was
corrected, not code made worse. State which in your report, and move the literal to whatever the
suite actually produces.
